stem: A plant shows a deficiency-like symptom while the supplied nutrient solution appears adequate, but root-zone pH is outside the intended range. What is the most defensible next interpretation?
choices: Nutrient availability may be limiting even when nutrient supply is present
The nutrient must be absent from the fertilizer
Visual symptoms alone prove a single-element deficiency
rationale: Symptoms should be interpreted with supply, pH, EC, and root-zone context. Adequate nominal supply does not guarantee root availability when root-zone conditions are unfavorable.
